answer: Johannes Gutenberg, a German goldsmith, is credited with inventing the printing press with movable type in Europe around 1440 [1][2]. The exact date isn't known. Some accounts link early experiments to Strasbourg around 1440, and by 1450 his press was running in Mainz [1][3]. His best-known work, the Gutenberg Bible, was printed between about 1452 and 1455 [1]. Movable type wasn't new, since it was already used in East Asia. What Gutenberg's press changed was speed: books could be printed much faster, which drove the spread of printing in Europe [2].
